newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Atlas Copco 9-month profit up, maintains forecast.
newsitem.headline: Atlas Copco 9-month profit up, maintains forecast.

text.p: Swedish industrial engineering group Atlas Copco reported a nine percent rise in profits on Thursday and said it was holding to its forecast that the full year would be better than 1995.
The manufacturer of compressors and other industrial machinery said the nine-month profit of 2.23 billion Swedish crowns ($338 million) was on three percent higher sales of 18.32 billion crowns.

"The previous forecast for 1996 for an improved result compared with the previous year is maintained," Atlas Copco said, adding that demand for its products in the near future was expected to be largely unchanged.

Orders received fell in most of the main European markets such as Germany, France and Britain, but positive sales trends were reported in Italy, Benelux and eastern Europe. East Asia, Australia and South America also showed better orders.

The weak demand in northern Europe particularly hit Atlas Copco's small and medium-sized compressors and power tools, but demand for large compressors, drill rigs, loaders and assembly systems improved.
The strengthening Swedish crown over the reporting period had a negative effect worth nine percent on conversion.
Atlas Copco's profit margin in the nine months improved to 12.2 percent from 11.6 percent one year ago.
